The reviewed audits rate ProfiniteCohomology Layers 2 and 6, the connecting map of Layer 9 and ProfiniteProPGroups Layer 3 as the finding says. The corestriction computation is right. For U of index 2 with t(U) = 1, t(σU) = σ and trivial 𝔽₂ coefficients, the words are ℓ_U(σ) = σ², ℓ_{σU}(σ) = 1, ℓ_U(τ) = τ and ℓ_{σU}(τ) = σ⁻¹τσ. So cor(χ)(σ) = χ(σ²) and cor(χ)(τ) = χ(τ) + χ(σ⁻¹τσ), which is (3.1)–(3.2) (p. 22) because σ² ∈ U. The notes of /21, /28, /36, /52 and /83 therefore describe built layers as plans, and a design that follows them would re-plan built objects. Medium is right.
Two parts of the claim are wrong, and the fix has to be settled item by item. Checked. The paper cites only Smith for this estimate:
- p. 63, in the case 1 < i ≤ k of the proof of Proposition 7.6 (page image): 'The large sieve implies that for all ε > 0 Σ_{x1∈X1} |Σ_{xi∈Xi} (x1/xi)| ≪_ε t_i · t_1^{3/4+ε}, see for example [42, Proposition 6.6]';
- p. 105: 'We will now repeatedly apply the large sieve, as for example presented in [42, Proposition 6.6]'.
Its only Heath-Brown entry is [22], the Selmer-groups paper (Invent. Math. 118 (1994)), cited once, in §1 (p. 3). In Smith, arXiv 1702.02325v2 (SHA-256 e768b5ad…a59e, the red team's hash), Proposition 6.6 (p. 62) is proved 'By [14, Lemma 3]'. That gives a second moment O(t′1·|X2| + t′1^{1/2}·t′2² log⁶ t′2), and Cauchy's inequality and quadratic reciprocity on the four classes mod 4 finish the proof. Smith's [14] is Jutila, 'On mean values of Dirichlet polynomials with real characters', Acta Arith. 27 (1975) 191–198 (Crossref, doi:10.4064/aa-27-1-191-198). So the attribution to Heath-Brown, Acta Arith. 72 (1995), is wrong everywhere the extraction makes it: item 189's note, route 5's reason, three places in route 1's brief (layer 5, the SV.2 import and the prerequisite papers), the prerequisites entry, the summary field ('Heath-Brown's large sieve for Legendre symbols in boxes (§7)') and the report. SV.2 stays the owner: RS-07 narrows it to large-sieve inequalities, and Jutila's lemma is one. Medium is right, because the route, the brief and the prerequisites ask for a much deeper theorem than the source uses.
One correction to the derivation in the claim. With x₁ as the outer variable, Cauchy–Schwarz leaves t₁^{3/4}t_i log³t_i. Proposition 7.6(ii) allows t_i ≤ t_k < e^{t₁^{c₂}}, so log³t_i can be as large as t₁^{3c₂}, which is not ≪ t₁^ε. The whole range t₁ < t_i comes from the other ordering, which reciprocity allows: with x_i outer the bound is t_i t₁^{1/2} + t_i^{3/4}t₁ log³t₁ ≪_ε t_i t₁^{3/4+ε}. That is how Smith's symmetric bound arises, and the finding's conclusion stands. The note's remark on the classical multiplicative large sieve is right: its second moment is ≪ (t₁² + t_i)|X_i|, which is enough only for t_i ≥ t₁^{3/2}.
Adjustments to the fix:
- (a) Item 189's note should name the ordering: x_i outer, after reciprocity on the four classes mod 4.
- (b) is void. Item 263's note names no Heath-Brown result ('the same bilinear Legendre-symbol large-sieve input as (7.11)'), so it stays.
- (d) must also replace the brief's third mention, in its list of prerequisite papers.
- The summary field and the report's §7, route 5 and prerequisite lines need the same correction.
- The item should not coalesce with PAPER-SKOROBOGATOV-SOFOS-23's Heath-Brown item at SV.2, which is a different and deeper statement.

Checked. Route 2 is a source of ClassicalArithmeticCompletion with stages ['ClassicalArithmeticCompletion:CA.4'] and items /2–/5, /9 and /12. Items 5 and 12 (d ∈ 𝒟⁻ iff the 2-Sylow subgroups of Cl⁺ and Cl agree, iff (√d) is narrowly trivial) and item 9 (the unit group has a unit of norm −1) all pass between integral solutions of x² − dy² = −1 and units of 𝒪_K of norm −1. Tau Ceti f790474 has one direction and the class-group criterion:
- NumberField.exists_norm_eq_neg_one_of_sq_sub_mul_sq_eq_neg_one (Quadratic/Norm.lean:108): a solution gives a unit of norm −1;
- NumberField.NarrowClassGroup.toClassGroup_injective_iff_exists_norm_eq_neg_one (Quadratic/Conjugation/NarrowClassGroup.lean:215).
The converse, from a unit of 𝒪_K to an integral solution, is the missing step. The CA packet puts the ℤ[√d]/𝒪_K comparison in CA.5, in the nodes zsqrtd-into-the-ring-of-integers, pell-solutions-are-norm-one-units and negative-pell-iff-unit-of-norm-minus-one. The last is stated for 'd > 1 squarefree, d ≢ 1 (mod 4)'. CA.4's nodes work in ℤ√d only. The paper's 𝒟 (p. 2) is the set of squarefree d > 0 whose prime factors are ≡ 1, 2 mod 4. Every odd member is therefore ≡ 1 (mod 4), and the node covers only the even members.
Both missing cases hold:
- d ≡ 1 (mod 8): a unit (a + b√d)/2 with a, b odd would need a² − db² = ±4, but a² − db² ≡ 0 (mod 8), so 𝒪_K^× ⊆ ℤ[√d];
- d ≡ 5 (mod 8): such a unit u of norm ν has u³ = (a(a² − 3ν) + b(a² − ν)√d)/2 ∈ ℤ[√d], with N(u³) = ν (for d = 5, ((1 + √5)/2)³ = 2 + √5).
Adding CA.5 is valid: it is a layer of the same roadmap, CA.4 → CA.5 is an atlas edge, and the Part II may import it. The CA packet is merged but unreviewed (review #532 open and blocked); the finding does not depend on its acceptance. Medium is right.
Adjustments to the fix:
- Route 2's reason should say that /2–/4 go to CA.4 and /5, /9 and /12 to CA.5.
- The sentence goes into item 9's note as well.
- The notes cite both built declarations, so that only the converse is missing.
- CA.5 joins the import list of route 1's brief and the report's route 2.

Checked, with the p. 30 page image. Lemma 4.5 stands on its own hypotheses: 'Let S be a set of squarefree integers all greater than 1. Assume that the decomposition group of (2) in the field K = ℚ({√x : x ∈ S}) is cyclic. Let k ≥ 1 be an integer and suppose that we are given raw cocycles ψ_{k+1}(x) for N(x) for each x ∈ S.' Nothing makes the cocycles non-zero. Definition 2.8 (p. 11) allows the zero sequence. By the definition on p. 6, L(φ) is the field of the largest normal open subgroup through which φ factors, so L(0) = ℚ. Proposition 2.5 (p. 10) puts ℚ(χ) inside L(ψ) only 'in case ψ(G_{ℚ(χ)}) ⊄ N[2]'. So the review's premise, 'K ⊆ ∏_x L(ψ_{k+1}(x))', fails in general.
The counterexample holds. 65 = 5·13 ≡ 1 (mod 8), so (2) splits in K = ℚ(√65). With k = 1 and ψ₂(65) = 0, the prime 5 ramifies in K but ∏L = ℚ, so its index is 1. The bound e ≤ 2 always holds: ∏L·K/K is unramified at the finite places, and inertia in Gal(K/ℚ) is cyclic at odd p by tameness and at (2) by hypothesis. It is also all the applications use (pp. 31–34, 47, 52). E12 now contradicts itself. Its correction ends 'The ramification index in the first sentence does equal 2, so nothing is wrong there', while its reason ends ''Equals 2' fails for trivial raw cocycles (L(0) = ℚ); only e ≤ 2 is ever used'. Low is right, because what gets built does not change.
Adjustments to the fix:
- (1) Drop '(as in every application)' from the restored text. Theorem 5.10's triples also start from 'Let a be a divisor of d₀' (p. 45), so they do not exclude zero cocycles either. Say instead that the applications use only 'at most 2'.
- (2) Item 104 should state the corrected bound, 'is at most 2', and mention the printed 'equals 2' as a remark, because §18 says items use the corrected statements.
- (3) The extraction's report also carries the strike, in its header and in the E12 paragraph. It should be corrected along with REV-PAPER-KOYMANS-PAGANO.md.

Checked. §2.3 (pp. 19–20) defines ⟨−,−⟩_{Art_s(A)} on 2^{s−1}A[2^s] × 2^{s−1}A^∨[2^s], with left kernel 2^s·A[2^{s+1}], as item 69 states. With item 211's convention rk_{2^k}A = dim 2^{k−1}A[2^k], the domain has dimension rk_{2^s}A and the left kernel has dimension rk_{2^{s+1}}A. So the pairing has rank rk_{2^s}A − rk_{2^{s+1}}A. The note's 'rk_{2^s} A = dim of 2^{s−1}A[2^s] minus the dimension of the left kernel' would force rk_{2^{s+1}}A = 0 for every A. For A = ℤ/4 and s = 1, A[2] and 2·A[4] are both {0, 2}; the note gives rk₂(ℤ/4) = 0, but it is 1. §8 uses the right form: Definition 8.6 (p. 80) takes the left kernel of Art_i, whose dimension is the 2^{i+1}-rank. The replacement sentence is right. Low is right, because only a note is wrong.

Checked, with the p. 28 page image. The set-up says only 'Let a be a divisor of d₀'. Remark 4.1 derives a > 0 from (4.1) but not a ≠ 1, and neither Definition 4.2 nor Theorem 4.6 adds it. Take a = 1 and ψ_{s+1}(x) = 0 for all x ∈ C − {x₀}. The zero sequence is a raw cocycle and (4.1) holds. The first two conditions of Definition 4.2 are sums of these cochains, and the last three involve only the p_i(h) and d₀, so the triple can be profitable. Theorem 4.6 then asserts an expansion map with support {χ_{p_i(1)p_i(2)}} ∪ {χ₁} and pointer χ₁ = 0, which Definition 2.12 (p. 14, 'a linearly independent finite set') excludes. The proof also applies Theorem 3.2 with pointer χ_a (p. 33), and §3.1 (p. 20) needs Ram(ℚ(χ_a)/ℚ) ≠ ∅.
Nothing downstream uses a = 1. §5 inherits the set-up, and §8.4 instantiates it only through the characters ψ₁(x, v) of non-zero kernel vectors v (p. 93), so a is a product of primes. 'Misprint, affects nothing' matches how the file records the omitted hypotheses of Lemma 2.13 (E5) and Lemma 6.10 (E27). Low is right.
Adjustments to the fix:
- Put 'a > 1' in item 98's statement, where a is introduced; items 107 and 108 may repeat it.
- In E52's reason, replace 'every use in §§5 and 8.4 has a > 1' with the sentence above about §5 and §8.4.

Checked, with the p. 53 page image, against Smith arXiv 1702.02325v2 (SHA-256 e768b5ad…a59e), the version the bibliography names (p. 110).
- (a) The proof of Lemma 6.3 reads 'This is [42, Lemma 4.1], where their d is our r and their r is our b'. v2 has no Lemma 4.1. Its §4 has Proposition 4.1 (pp. 36–37), Definition 4.2, Proposition 4.3 and Proposition 4.4, which is on p. 40 (not p. 38, as the evidence says). Its only numbered lemma is Lemma 5.1.
- (b) Proposition 4.1 begins 'Take d ≥ 2 to be an integer, take 2^{−d−1} > δ > 0', with r ≤ (log n / 5 log δ^{−1})^{1/(d−1)}. Lemma 6.3 omits r ≥ 2 although its exponent 1/(r − 1) needs it. Its one application (p. 91) has |S′| ≥ m − 1 ≥ 2, so both slips affect nothing. §16's 'exact statement, with every hypothesis' puts r ≥ 2 in item 154's statement.
- (c) Item 159's check succeeds for |S| ≥ 2. Smith's Proposition 4.4 takes S as in his Definition 4.2 (|S| ≥ 2) and works in one fibre of π_{[d]−S}. Add(X, S) is the direct sum over the fibres of π_{[r]−S}, so g can be chosen fibre by fibre, and the errors sum to ε|X|. KP's size hypothesis implies Smith's (4.3), since |S| ≤ r. KP's C(𝔄) is an intersection over the codimension-1 faces, and it equals Smith's Z_S, because the recursive definition of C_T (Definition 6.1) makes every face of an accepted cube accepted.
Low is right.
Adjustment to the fix: item 159's note should cite Smith's Proposition 4.4 on p. 40 and say that the derivation covers |S| ≥ 2.
One further observation for the fixer. Proposition 6.6 as printed allows S = ∅, and there it fails. C(𝔄) = X, acceptability forces C_∅^acc = X and F = g, and for X a single point |F⁻¹(0)| ∈ {0, 1} is never within ε < ½ of ½, while the size hypothesis is empty. Its one application (p. 106) has |S| ≥ m ≥ 3. So item 159 should carry S ≠ ∅, or |S| ≥ 2 as Smith has it, and this may be recorded with E53–E54 as a misprint affecting nothing.

Checked, with the p. 3 page image, which reads: 'one can use Theorem 8.1 to give an explicit error term for the rate of convergence in Theorem 1.1. The implied constant is effectively computable.' That needs Theorem 8.1 with effective constants for every m ≥ 2. The paper proves it only for m ≥ 3 and takes m = 2 from [8, Theorem 6.1] (p. 75). It notes (p. 59) that for [8, Theorem 5.15] 'it was not shown that the implied constant is effectively computable', and §7 makes only the 4-rank input effective, after Watkins [46] (p. 61).
[8] is arXiv 1908.01752, whose only version is v1 (SHA-256 385c90c9…698c8d, the red team's hash). There Theorem 6.1 comes from Proposition 6.3, whose proof runs through Theorem 5.9 and Propositions 6.6 and 6.10, resting on Propositions 5.7 and 5.10. The proof of Proposition 5.7 (p. 22) uses 'By Siegel's theorem, for D₁ sufficiently large'. The chain in the claim ('Proposition 6.3 → Propositions 5.12–5.13 → Proposition 5.7') is slightly off, since 5.12 and 5.13 are counting results that do not use Siegel's theorem, but the conclusion stands. The published version, Forum Math. Sigma 10 (2022) e46 (doi:10.1017/fms.2022.40, retitled 'The 8-rank of the narrow class group and the negative Pell equation'), keeps Theorem 6.1 and the same Siegel step. So the p. 3 claim is asserted without adequate proof. It is a gap in a remark, affecting nothing, and low is right.
Adjustments to E55:
- Its correction should cite Watkins [47], 'Notes on 4-Selmer and 8-class ranks', as the effective source for m = 2, rather than assert that the §7 device repairs it. The paper cites [47] on p. 76 only for its error term, but its §1.1.1 says 'our results here are effective' of its 8-rank theorem for Gaussian discriminants.
- It should add that the box form of the m = 2 step, which E41 requires, must be effective too.
- The pointer goes into item 214's note (in the finding's 'where' but not its fix) as well as item 8's.

Checked. '(issues file)' appears in fourteen item notes. Eleven point to existing entries (11 → E2, 41 → E3, 46 → E4, 56 → E5, 61 → E6, 67 → E7, 82 → E8, and 78, 80, 90 and 96 → E9); items 13, 23 and 93 have none.
- Item 13: (1.3) on p. 3 (page image) prints ⟨bπ_k(d), χ_a + χ_{π₁(d)}⟩ with C = {d₀} × {p_{1,1}, p_{1,2}} × ⋯ × {p_{k,1}, p_{k,2}}. §1.1 fixes π_i as the projection to the i-th factor, so as printed π₁(d) = d₀ and π_k(d) ∈ {p_{k−1,1}, p_{k−1,2}}, while the Frobenius elements on the right are at p_{k,1} and p_{k,2}. Indexing from 0 is meant. That is a misprint, and since §18 says mistakes are recorded and never silently corrected, it should get an entry (affects nothing: (1.3) is an informal sketch).
- Item 23: N(φ), the subgroup, is defined on p. 6 and used only there, to define L(φ); from p. 9 on, N(χ) is the twisted module. That is an overloaded notation, not a mistake, so the tag should just be deleted.
- Item 93: the note's claim is wrong, as the red team says. Proposition 3.3 gives N_{ℚ(A)/ℚ(B)}(α_{i,A}) = α_{i,B} modulo squares for all B ⊆ A. Applied to each T ⊆ A, by transitivity of norms, it gives σ_a(α_{h,T}) ≡ α_{h,T}·α_{h,T−{a}} for a ∈ T, while σ_a fixes α_{h,T} for a ∉ T. Composing over the generators σ_a of Gal(ℚ(A)/ℚ) ≅ 𝔽₂^A gives σ⁻¹(α_{h,A}) ≡ α_{h,A}γ_h with γ_h in the span of the α_{h,T}, T ⊊ A, which is the step on p. 25. The replacement text should include the transitivity step, which the claim leaves implicit.
Low is right. An optional tidy-up is to replace the eleven other tags by their entry ids.

Checked. §18 says: 'The file therefore records what was read, alongside sourceIssues, and scripts/check_errata.py requires it as soon as any finding quotes a stated result.' E4 and E7 have affects 'a stated result', and the file has no sourceVersions. The reading is described only in source.readSections (v1, SHA-256 c7a93ffe…50cbd, fetched 23 September 2026). This is not a lapse by the extraction, which is dated 23 September. The rule entered PROTOCOL.md on 24 September (commit eab24c32), and scripts/check_paper.py does not enforce it. On 30 September 2026 arXiv still lists only v1, with no journal reference, and Crossref has no record of the paper, so there is still nothing to collate against. Low is right.
The fix stands, with one warning and one correction.
- Warning: add only the preprint entry, with the TeX-source hash and a note that E4, E7 and the locators are to be collated against the Acta version when it appears. Do not add a 'published' entry for the unread Acta text: collation.provenance returns 'published' as soon as any entry has that kind, and the paper would drop off the worklist.
- Correction: the evidence says the paper is 'not listed there only because its papers.json citation has no year'. That is not right. collation.published_exists is false because the record's link is Koymans's web page, and a year in the citation does not change that (tested with 'Acta Mathematica (2027)' and 'Acta Math. 240 (2027)'); only a publisher DOI link does. Once the paper appears, papers.json needs that link for collation to list it.
